defs.def: a talk that is given to a group of people to teach them about a particular subject, often as part of a university or college course （通常指大学里的）讲座，讲课，演讲

ex.s: Once in a lecture, the professor tried repeating my name after me over and over in front of thirty classmates.
ex.t: 有一次上课时，教授当着三十个同学的面一遍又一遍地跟着我重复我的名字。

ex.s: I realized that if I didn’t stop, the entire lecture would be ruined.
ex.t: 因为我非常喜欢它，我以为自己擅长美术。

ex.s: Be sure to schedule set times to watch your lectures, read materials and contribute to online discussion boards.
ex.t: 一定要安排固定时间观看课程讲座、阅读资料并参与在线讨论板。

ex.s: Many instructors continue to teach using traditional lectures, which lead to lower success rates.
ex.t: 许多教师继续使用传统的讲授式教学，导致成功率较低。

ex.s: Attending a lecture.
ex.t: 参加讲座。

ex.s: Class activities will vary from day to day, but students must be ready to complete short in-class writings or tests drawn directly from assigned readings or notes from the previous class' lecture/discussion, so it is important to take careful notes during class.
ex.t: 课堂活动每天都会有所不同，但学生必须准备好完成简短的课堂写作或测试，这些内容直接来自指定阅读材料或上一堂课的讲座/讨论笔记，因此上课时仔细记笔记很重要。

ex.s: They are held in the Lecture Room.
ex.t: 它们在报告厅展出。

ex.s: Admission to lectures is free.
ex.t: 听讲座免费入场。

ex.s: Travelling to conferences, lectures, workshops, and the like frequently by plane  ____37____（view） as important for scientists to get together and exchange information.
ex.t: 乘飞机频繁参加会议、讲座、研讨会等活动____37____（view）被认为是科学家聚集和交流信息的重要方式。

ex.s: It’s an opportunity to deepen your understanding of the key points from lecture materials while you are applying your skills to solve problems.
ex.t: 这是一个在你运用技能解决问题的同时加深你对讲座材料关键点的理解的机会。

ex.s: Lectures on a balanced life.
ex.t: 关于平衡生活的讲座。

ex.s: The barber, not recognising him, asked if he had a ticket to the lecture.
ex.t: 理发师没有认出他，问他有没有讲座的门票。

ex.s: I always have to stand when that fellow lectures!” 3 Like Twain, but on the other side of the world, Lin Yutang was soon to become famous for his unique brand of humour.
ex.t: 每次那个家伙讲课我都不得不站着！与马克·吐温一样，但在世界的另一边，林语堂很快就因其独特的幽默风格而闻名。

ex.s: A typical lecture often starts with addressing the topic directly.
ex.t: 一场典型的讲座通常以直接讨论主题开头。

defs.def: a long angry talk that sb gives to one person or a group of people because they have done sth wrong （冗长的）教训，训斥，谴责
to give a talk or a series of talks to a group of people on a subject, especially as a way of teaching in a university or college （尤指在大学里）开讲座，讲授，讲课

ex.s: I guess I was better than the others, for Miss Chevalier asked a while later, “Addie, I was wondering if you would recite the whole poem to the Saturday evening’s club.” She said a famous professor was going to give a lecture about the poet, and a presentation of that poem would be a fresh way to start.
ex.t: 我想我比其他人都好，因为过了一会儿谢瓦利埃小姐问：“艾迪，我在想你能不能在周六晚上的俱乐部上背诵整首诗。”她说一位著名教授将要做一个关于这位诗人的讲座，而朗诵那首诗会是一个新颖的开场方式。

ex.s: It is my great pleasure to give a lecture here on behalf of the Be at One with Nature Association.
ex.t: 我很荣幸代表与自然融为一体协会在这里发表演讲。

ex.s: The lecture is one of the oldest teaching methods, and is still widely used today.
ex.t: 讲课是最古老的教学方法之一，至今仍被广泛使用。

defs.def: to criticize sb or tell them how you think they should behave, especially when it is done in an annoying way （尤指恼人地）指责，训斥，告诫

ex.s: To try a new way to warm up the coming lecture.
ex.t: 尝试一种新方法来为即将到来的讲座做热身。
